_comment: Shared fixtures for the content-paths <-> _paths mirror pair.
tests/test_paths_mirror.py. Neither side owns this file; a change to either
implementation that is not matched on the other fails a test here.
WHY THIS EXISTS. content-paths.ts (569 lines) and _paths.py (412 lines) both
answer 'where does this book live on disk'. Until 2026-07-26 nothing checked
they agreed - the contract was a prose comment in each file plus a rule in
CLAUDE.md. If the two break a tie differently, the Astro site and the pipeline
operate on DIFFERENT DIRECTORIES FOR THE SAME BOOK, silently. That is worse
than a crash, because nothing surfaces it.
Modelled on anchor-key.fixtures.json, the one mirror pair that was already
pinned. Three sections because there are three distinct failure modes:
vocabulary   - an enum extended on one side only
pure_cases   - regex/casing dialect drift (JS \d is ASCII, Python's is not)
layout_cases - the two resolution ladders disagreeing about precedence
layout_cases are declarative: each harness materialises `tree` in its own temp
dir, points PODCAST_FACTORY_ROOT at it, and asserts the same answer. Paths in
`expect` are repo-root-relative so the two languages compare equal without

resolve_bucket_cases.why: no signal at all defaults to Islamic

vol_dir_cases.why: JS \d is ASCII-only, Python's is Unicode-aware. Arabic-Indic digits must NOT match on either side.

composite_slug_cases.why: greedy work part - the LAST vol-NN wins
Arabic-Indic digits must not parse as a volume on either side

layout_cases.name: type-first: a flat book in a bucket resolves to its bucket dir
type-first: buckets are searched in declared order, Islamic first
type-first WINS over a legacy dir carrying the same slug
composite volume slug resolves under a real work parent
composite slug does NOT resolve when the parent has no work.yml marker
a flat book whose name ends in -vol-N resolves as itself, not as a volume

layout_cases.why: THE PRECEDENCE CASE. Python scanned every category under drafts, then every category under published, and only then fell back to flat drafts. TypeScript scanned drafts categories, then flat drafts, then published categories - so this tree resolved to two DIFFERENT directories depending on which side asked. Found and fixed 2026-07-26.
layout_cases.name: flat drafts vs categorised published: categorised published wins

layout_cases.why: Python guarded flat resolution against a slug that is itself a category name; TypeScript guarded only the drafts stage.
layout_cases.name: a category name is never resolved as a flat book

layout_cases.why: BOOKS and LECTURES are legacy CONTAINERS, not books - iter_content skips both when enumerating. content-paths.ts guarded both; _paths.py guarded only BOOKS. Aligned 2026-07-26.
layout_cases.name: the LECTURES container is never resolved as a flat book

layout_cases.why: Python had a drafts/BOOKS/<slug> fallback that TypeScript lacked entirely. Skipped on a case-insensitive filesystem (macOS default), where drafts/BOOKS and drafts/books are the same directory and the category loop legitimately matches first - the outcome would differ by platform, not by implementation, which is not what this pair is pinning.
layout_cases.name: legacy nested orphan drafts/BOOKS/<slug>
an unknown slug resolves to nothing

layout_cases.why: Load-bearing: _paths skips _-prefixed names to tell plumbing from books. If one side stopped skipping, content/_system would enumerate as a book.
layout_cases.name: underscore-prefixed dirs are plumbing, never content

status_cases.name: a missing status key falls back to draft
an unreadable state file falls back to draft, never throws
